short_answer: OddsShark is no longer a separate site. On 20 Nov 2026 oddsshark.com answered with a permanent redirect, and its old NFL computer picks address pointed to covers.com/picks/nfl, under a page headed "Odds Shark is now part of Covers." Covers' About page says it is part of the Genius Sports group and names CS Media Ltd as the operator. Genius Sports, a sports data company, agreed in February 2026 to buy Legend, the media network behind Covers, in a deal reported at up to $1.2 billion, and trade press reported it closed in May 2026.

The picks are free. The NFL page shows a computer projected score and a spread, total and moneyline side for every game, under the heading "New Computer Picks powered by Odds Shark," but no results table and no method. Archived copies of the old OddsShark pages from January and June 2025 did show a last 100 games table. We checked those numbers: in January 2025 the NFL computer was ahead on moneylines and spreads but behind on totals, and in June 2025 the NBA computer was behind on spreads at opening lines. Most of the dollar figures match a flat -110 calculation; two NFL figures do not.

Covers earns from betting offers. The odds beside the computer picks link through Covers redirect links to prediction market apps such as Kalshi, Novig, ProphetX and Polymarket, a Kalshi "Exclusive $60 Bonus" banner sits on the page, and in 2025 the old OddsShark pages carried paid "Sponsored Picks" boxes from pick sellers. Treat OddsShark picks as free content from an affiliate publisher, not a proven edge.
pricing_intro: Nothing on the OddsShark or Covers picks pages we opened on 20 Nov 2026 was for sale, as on our 7 Nov 2026 check. Covers' About page says its core products are free, with no signup or subscription.
pricing: Computer picks, powered by Odds Shark
App Store listing promotes expert picks, best bets and parlays
guarantee: There is nothing to guarantee because the picks are free. The real cost to a reader is the bets placed on them, and none of the pages we opened promised results.

Covers' terms, updated 5 August 2026, say its content is "provided for your non-commercial entertainment and enjoyment" and disclaim that results will be "accurate or reliable." They give a postal address for CS Media Ltd in Post Falls, Idaho, and name no governing jurisdiction.

claims_note: How we checked. The live Covers page has no results, so we opened the last archived copies of the old OddsShark NFL computer picks page (16 Jan 2025, end of the NFL regular season) and NBA computer picks page (3 Jun 2025, NBA Finals). Each showed a "Computer Picks Results, Last 100 Games" table with records and dollar results at $100 a unit, at opening and closing lines. For each spread and total row we computed the profit a bettor would make risking $100 a bet at -110 and compared it with the printed figure.

Six of the eight spread and total figures land within about $60 of our flat -110 math, and four within $5, so the table appears to be computed the way it says. Two NFL opening line figures do not fit: the spread row printed $1,227 where 60-39 at -110 gives about $1,555, and the totals row printed -$383 where 49-46 gives about -$145. The page did not explain the gap, which could come from worse opening prices than -110.

The tables show why one headline number misleads. The NFL computer looked strong against the spread in January 2025 (60.6% at opening lines, 57.1% at closing lines), but its totals lost money. Five months later the NBA computer lost against the spread at opening lines (48.5%) while its totals won. Its moneyline picks won 64% of the time in the NBA table and still made only $61 over 100 games, because picking favorites pays little. A 100 game window is also short: it rolls forward every day, so a reader sees whatever the latest stretch happened to be.

Old OddsShark pick history is hard to find now that its pages redirect to Covers. Beyond these two archived snapshots we found no archive of past OddsShark computer picks with results, and no outside party that graded them.
record: What is independently verifiable: nothing about OddsShark's picks. We found no outside monitor, contest or regulator record of its computer or analyst picks. Covers runs its own free contests, which we cover in our Covers expert picks review, but those grade Covers users, not the OddsShark computer.

What is the seller's own marketing: in 2025 the old OddsShark pages showed a rolling last 100 games table for the computer, and analyst picks carried a time stamp such as "Bet placed at 12:34 pm ET on Tuesday, January 14," which is good practice. On 20 Nov 2026 the Covers NFL page showed computer projections for every Week 11 game but no results table, no method text and no visible analyst picks, only an "Expert Picks" tab.

Legal history: our searches found no court or regulator action involving OddsShark. Covers' terms name CS Media Ltd, with a postal address in Post Falls, Idaho. We could not confirm who owned OddsShark before it moved into Covers or exactly when the move happened; the trademark lookup we tried refused automated access.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition neither the OddsShark computer nor any Covers analyst is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: free computer picks on spreads and totals have to clear the same bar as paid ones. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: OddsShark itself has almost no customer footprint we could find: its Trustpilot page had no reviews and it has no app of its own in the US App Store. Because its picks now live on Covers, we also read Covers reviews. Those mostly praise the free contests and research tools, and only one we found speaks to whether the picks win.

customers.text: We found no paying buyer of OddsShark picks, because they are free, and very few posts that judge them at all. On the Covers forum in June 2024 two members called oddsshark.com a solid free stats site and one liked its head to head database while wishing it had day of the week splits; a few days later another member called it useless, saying it was full of its own predictions and lacked basics such as game logs and bullpen stats. A Reddit poster in 2024 said they were betting $20 on OddsShark's NFL picks, with no follow up. The only review that speaks to results, a May 2026 Trustpilot review of Covers, says tracked computer and expert picks hit below 50 percent. Reviews of Covers as a whole are strongly positive (4.7 on Trustpilot and on the App Store), but they praise contests, layout and prize payouts, not pick results.
Trustpilot showed an OddsShark profile, claimed in Dec 2024 and listed in Canada, with 0 reviews.
SmartCustomer showed an unclaimed oddsshark.com page with 0 reviews.

A Covers reviewer on Trustpilot said they had tracked the site's computer picks and expert picks in baseball, basketball and football and found overall pick accuracy below 50%. They did not post their log, and we do not know whether the computer they tracked was the Odds Shark model now labeled on the page.
A short Covers review on Trustpilot praised the content and the free picks, with no mention of results.
A reviewer who said they had used Covers for 15 years credited it with teaching them about money management and pick strategy, and thanked handicappers who share opinions free. They gave no results.

Covers' Trustpilot page showed 4.7 from 264 reviews, 88% five star and 3% one star, with a note that the company had not invited reviews recently. The recent reviews mostly praise free contests and quick prize payouts rather than the picks.

The free Covers iPhone app, published by CS Media LTD, showed 4.7 out of 5 from 548 ratings on 20 Nov 2026, up from 471 on 7 Nov. Its description promotes expert picks, best bets and parlays. The visible reviews, dated May and September with no year shown, praise the clean layout and the free picks; several drew replies from the developer.

In the same Covers forum thread about free stats sites, a member called oddsshark.com useless for baseball research, saying it was filled with its own prediction content and lacked game logs, bullpen numbers and splits against left handed pitching. Another member agreed.

A Reddit poster in r/sportsbetting said they had looked at the NFL picks on OddsShark and were letting $20 ride on them. The only reply posted a payout figure without saying what it was for, and nobody reported a result.
Our searches found no TheRX, SBR or Covers forum thread that evaluates OddsShark's computer picks record, no Better Business Bureau profile, and no OddsShark app in the US App Store.

conflicts: Covers, which now runs OddsShark, earns from betting operators. On 20 Nov 2026 the odds beside the computer picks linked through Covers redirect links to Kalshi, Novig, ProphetX and Polymarket, a Kalshi "Exclusive $60 Bonus" banner sat on the page, and the covers.com/oddsshark page listed bonus code pages for thirteen sportsbooks and twelve prediction market apps.

In 2025 the old OddsShark computer picks pages placed "Sponsored Picks" boxes from paid pick sellers, including Doc's Premium Picks, Wunderdog Picks and Outlier Premium Data, right beside its own free picks, and its menu carried a "Picks Service Reviews" section. A site that sells placement to pick sellers and also reviews them has a conflict a reader should weigh.

Covers' DraftKings promo page, when we read it on 7 Nov 2026, said the offer applies when you sign up "through our exclusive link," labelled it "Sponsored by DK" and a Covers and DraftKings partnership, and said affiliate links are disclosed. We saw no such disclosure next to the picks themselves, and the Covers terms contain no affiliate disclosure.

Covers belongs to Genius Sports, a sports data company listed on the New York Stock Exchange. Trade press described Legend, the network Genius bought, as a gaming affiliate business "built to monetize attention" with 320 million visits a year.
strengths: Free, with no signup needed to see computer projections and picks for every game on the board.
Computer picks give projected scores, so you can compare them with your own numbers rather than just tail a side.
When the old OddsShark pages published results, they tracked both opening and closing lines over a rolling 100 games, and our check found most figures consistent with flat -110 math.
Covers names its operator, CS Media Ltd, its postal address and its parent group.
Analyst picks on the old pages carried an exact time stamp, which is what a buyer should demand of any seller.
concerns: No results table, method text or season record for the computer was visible on the Covers page on 7 Nov or 20 Nov 2026.
The last archived tables we found showed losing columns (NFL totals in January 2025, NBA spreads at opening lines in June 2025) beside winning ones.
Two archived NFL dollar figures do not match the records printed beside them.
Prediction market and sportsbook links, a $60 bonus banner and, in 2025, paid sponsored picks sat right beside the free picks.
The move into Covers makes old OddsShark pick history hard to find, and customer reviews are about Covers' contests and tools, not about whether these picks win.
checklist: Before following any free computer pick, find its results at closing lines over at least a full season. If the page shows none, treat the pick as a projection.
Count dollars, not wins. A 64% moneyline record can still make almost nothing when it backs favorites.
Check whether a pick still holds at the line you can get now; the archived tables show opening and closing results can differ by hundreds of dollars over 100 games.
Write down each pick yourself with the time and the price, then grade it after a few hundred picks.
Do not sign up for a sportsbook or prediction market app because a link sits beside a pick. Read who earns from that link.
Prediction market and offshore offers are not regulated the same way as state licensed sportsbooks. Check the law where you live.
faq: Yes, as a real media brand: OddsShark is now part of Covers, which names CS Media Ltd as its operator and says it belongs to the Genius Sports group. That says nothing about whether its picks win, which we could not verify.
Nothing. The computer and analyst picks we saw on 20 Nov 2026 were free with no subscription; the site earns from sportsbook and prediction market offers instead.
Does OddsShark have a verified record?

No. We found no outside record, and the results table the old pages described was not on the Covers page when we checked. Archived 2025 tables showed a mix of winning and losing columns over 100 game windows, and Watchdog has no graded record for it.

On 20 Nov 2026 oddsshark.com returned a permanent redirect to Covers, and its computer picks pages now sit on covers.com under "Computer Picks powered by Odds Shark." An archived copy from June 2025 still showed OddsShark as its own site, with a 2008 to 2025 copyright.
Its pages are part of Covers, operated by CS Media Ltd. Covers is part of Genius Sports, which closed its purchase of Covers owner Legend in May 2026 according to trade press.

It is free, so you pay only with the bets you place, and you get projected scores and sides for every game. What is unproven is whether following them beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110, and the links beside them earn the site money when you sign up with a book or app.
